concerns.concern: The headline velocity anomaly rests on a sparse temperature series of only seven points, with none between 150 and 200 K. The 5.5% drop is defined from a single paramagnetic point, so the transition temperature and the shape of the anomaly are unresolved. Dense steps and both cooling and warming sweeps are requested.
concerns.quote: There is no point between 150 and 200 K. The "5.5% drop" is defined from a single PM maximum at 200 K

concerns.concern: The data appear to come from a single flake at a single wavevector, so reproducibility is not shown. At least two more flakes, ideally of different thickness, with the flake-to-flake spread, are requested.
concerns.quote: at least two additional flakes, ideally of different thickness, with flake-to-flake spread shown

concerns.concern: The authors' own DFT/FEM calculation gives a shift ten times smaller than measured (0.54%). Comparing a non-magnetic state with the AFM state should overestimate the effect, so appealing to finite-temperature effects does not explain the shortfall.
concerns.quote: The AFM-vs-NM FEM shift is 0.54%, ten times smaller than measured.

concerns.concern: The room-temperature velocity in the temperature-dependence data differs by about 4% from the dispersion data at the same wavevector under nominally identical conditions. This unexplained discrepancy is comparable to the claimed magnetic effect.
concerns.quote: This ~4% discrepancy under nominally identical conditions is comparable to the claimed magnetic effect. It is unexplained

concerns.concern: There is no in-situ reference, such as a substrate mode or measurements at several angles. Thermal tilt of the sample would change the wavevector and could produce percent-level apparent velocity changes.
concerns.quote: Since Δq/q = cotθ·Δθ, a 1° change at θ = 35° gives ~2.5%.

concerns.concern: Adsorbate or ice deposition on cooling could mass-load the surface and soften the Rayleigh wave. The strong loss of scattered intensity on cooling is consistent with such deposition.
concerns.quote: The pronounced loss of scattered intensity on cooling (Fig. 4a) is consistent with deposition on the sample or window.

concerns.concern: Laser heating is uncontrolled: BMS laser power and spot size are not given and NiPS3 absorbs at 532 nm. The effective sample temperature and apparent T_N are therefore unknown. A laser-power dependence is requested.
concerns.quote: The effective sample temperature, and hence the apparent T_N, is unknown.

concerns.concern: The low-temperature spectra are weak and broad, and the fitted shift is only a fraction of the linewidth. The background model and the origin of the error bars are not described.
concerns.quote: The fitted shift (~0.2 GHz) is a fraction of the linewidth. The background model and the origin of the error bars are not described.

concerns.concern: The dominant constant c44 is identical in the two DFT phases. The experiment would therefore require a ~10% softening of interlayer shear (or a large change in c33) that theory does not reproduce and that is not linked to the exchange. A quantitative inversion of the data is requested.
concerns.quote: Yet DFT gives c44 identical in both phases (9.7 GPa). The experiment therefore implies a ~10% softening of the interlayer shear stiffness

concerns.concern: Clamped spontaneous magnetostriction below T_N could create built-in stress in the film. Through higher-order elastic constants, this stress could change the velocity independently of the dynamic magnetoelastic renormalization.
concerns.quote: For a film clamped to SiO2, this strain cannot relax in-plane, so a built-in stress develops below T_N.

concerns.concern: Differential thermal contraction between NiPS3 and the Si/SiO2 substrate adds a temperature-dependent strain that could contribute to the velocity change.
concerns.quote: Differential thermal contraction between NiPS3 and Si/SiO2 adds a further temperature-dependent strain.

concerns.concern: Changes in the compliance of the film-substrate interface could also contribute to the velocity change and are not considered.
concerns.quote: Changes in interface compliance would also enter.

concerns.concern: The 3% velocity rise between 300 and 200 K is attributed to anharmonic stiffening without any fitted model. The size of the anomaly therefore depends on an unstated baseline.
concerns.quote: This is large for 100 K and is not fitted to any model, so the magnitude of the "anomaly" depends on an unstated baseline.

concerns.concern: Strong short-range magnetic correlations well above T_N in quasi-2D NiPS3 may themselves cause part of the high-temperature velocity trend. These fluctuation contributions are not discussed.
concerns.quote: Part of the 300→200 K trend may itself be magnetic.

concerns.concern: T_N of the measured flake is assumed from the bulk value rather than measured on the same flake under BMS illumination. This is inconsistent with the 150 K point being labelled as the drop.
concerns.quote: The bulk value of ~155 K is used, but the 150 K point is labelled as the drop.

concerns.concern: The BMS linewidth and intensity versus temperature are not reported. A damping anomaly at T_N would give corroborating evidence and an independent T_N.
concerns.quote: The BMS linewidth and intensity versus temperature should be reported in any case.

concerns.concern: The phenomenological model c_eff = c0 − λ²χ uses the uniform susceptibility, which is not the standard result for an antiferromagnet. A proper Landau or magnetoelastic treatment is requested.
concerns.quote: The expression c_eff = c0 − λ²χ_m with the uniform susceptibility is not the standard result for an antiferromagnet.

concerns.concern: The model's claimed prediction of a 5.5% velocity decrease is circular, because 5.5% is the input rather than an output.
concerns.quote: is circular: 5.5% is the input, not an output.

concerns.concern: The relation Δc/c ≈ 2Δv/v assumes the Rayleigh velocity scales with a single film modulus. This fails in a heterostructure where the substrate participates.
concerns.quote: That is not true in a heterostructure with substrate participation at qh ≈ 3.

concerns.concern: No microscopic estimate of the magnetoelastic coupling is given, for example from strain derivatives of exchange energies or from measured magnetostriction. It is therefore not shown that the predicted step is compatible with the implied change in c44 or c33.
concerns.quote: a microscopic estimate of the coupling, for example from strain derivatives of E_AFM − E_FM in DFT, or from measured NiPS3 magnetostriction

concerns.concern: The crystallographic orientation is not uniquely determined, because cleavage edges at 60° do not distinguish the a axis from [110]-type directions. Measurements with q along a as well as b are requested.
concerns.quote: Cleavage edges at 60° in the pseudo-hexagonal lattice do not uniquely distinguish a from the [110]-type directions.

concerns.concern: Zigzag order can form three domain orientations that the laser spot averages over, whereas the DFT tensor assumes a single domain. The Néel vector or domain orientation should be determined on the measured flake.
concerns.quote: Zigzag order can form three domain orientations, and the BMS spot averages over several microns.

concerns.concern: The calculated room-temperature frequency differs from experiment by about 10%, which exceeds the effect being explained. Calling this close agreement is overstated.
concerns.quote: This exceeds the effect being explained, so "close agreement" is overstated.

concerns.concern: Calling the effect 'giant' and 'rarely reported' is overstated. Several-percent ultrasonic anomalies at T_N are well known in conventional antiferromagnets, and the abstract's claim that theory reproduces the shift should be tempered.
concerns.quote: "Giant" and "rarely reported" need quantitative comparison.

concerns.concern: Prior reports of mechanical signatures of T_N in MPS3 materials are not cited or discussed: nanomechanical resonators (Šiškins 2020) and membrane magnetostriction (Houmes 2023).
concerns.quote: Mechanical signatures of T_N in MPS3 have been reported before.

concerns.concern: The claim that optical phonons are insensitive to magnetic order is undermined because the 255 cm⁻¹ Raman linewidth visibly changes near T_N.
concerns.quote: the 255 cm⁻¹ FWHM in Fig. 2d shows a visible change near T_N.

concerns.concern: The absence of the reported ~176 cm⁻¹ Raman splitting may reflect domain averaging or thickness rather than weak spin-phonon coupling.
concerns.quote: may reflect domain averaging or thickness, linking back to concern 7, rather than weak coupling.

concerns.concern: Comparing an absolute Raman shift with a fractional acoustic velocity change is not done on a common footing. Fractional shifts and coupling constants should be compared instead.
concerns.quote: Please compare fractional shifts and coupling constants on a common footing.

concerns.concern: The Raman anharmonic model, its fit range (which should exclude T < T_N) and its free parameters are not given.
concerns.quote: The anharmonic model, its fit range (it should exclude T < T_N), and the free parameters are not given.

concerns.concern: The FEM finds several branches and a slow-on-fast film should support Sezawa modes at these qh, yet these modes are absent from the spectra without explanation.
concerns.quote: At qh ≈ 2.6–4 a slow-on-fast film should support Sezawa modes, and the FEM finds several branches. Why are they absent from the spectra?

concerns.concern: The statement of Loudon's ripple-scattering rule is inaccurate, and the elasto-optic contribution may matter for an absorbing film. A computed BMS cross-section for the FEM branches is requested.
concerns.quote: The ripple mechanism requires surface-normal displacement, and shear-horizontal modes are also perpendicular but do not ripple.

concerns.concern: The DFT omits Hubbard U and spin-orbit coupling, and the non-magnetic state is likely metallic. A disordered-local-moment, SQS or FM comparison would be a better paramagnetic proxy.
concerns.quote: No Hubbard U or spin–orbit coupling is mentioned. NiPS3 normally requires DFT+U for a realistic gap and moment

concerns.concern: The stated supercell dimensions are inconsistent with the conventional C2/m cell. The authors should specify the cell, the spin arrangement and whether the structure was symmetrized.
concerns.quote: A "1×4×2 supercell" of 11.499 × 19.914 × 12.308 Å does not match the conventional C2/m cell

concerns.concern: The relaxed lattice parameters are not compared with experiment.
concerns.quote: Please compare the relaxed lattice parameters with experiment.

concerns.concern: Convergence of the soft elastic constants with respect to strain amplitude, k-mesh and smearing is not justified.
concerns.quote: Please justify convergence of the soft constants (c44 ≈ 10 GPa) with respect to strain amplitude (0.015), k-mesh (3×2×3) and smearing.

concerns.concern: The computed elastic constants are not compared with published NiPS3 elastic constants.
concerns.quote: Please compare with published NiPS3 elastic constants.

concerns.concern: Key FEM inputs are missing: NiPS3 density, SiO2 and Si constants, Si orientation, the rotation of the monoclinic tensor, and convergence with Si depth.
concerns.quote: how the monoclinic tensor was rotated into a frame with z normal to the layers (β ≈ 107°, which matters for c15, c25, c35, c46)

concerns.concern: The room-temperature velocities are not compared with the authors' own earlier MPS3 BMS data.
concerns.quote: Please compare the RT velocities with the authors' own earlier MPS3 BMS data (Ref. 36).

concerns.concern: Ref. 49 concerns optical spin-phonon constants, and its relevance to elastic renormalization is stated too loosely.
concerns.quote: Its relevance to elastic renormalization should be stated more carefully.

concerns.concern: An 80 K spectrum shown in Fig. 4a does not appear in the velocity plot of Fig. 4b.
concerns.quote: Fig. 4a shows an 80 K spectrum that does not appear in Fig. 4b.

concerns.concern: The paper does not state whether frequencies are averaged over Stokes and anti-Stokes peaks or how the interferometer was calibrated at each temperature. The AFM thickness uncertainty, which enters the FEM dispersion, is also not given.
concerns.quote: Please state whether frequencies are averaged over Stokes and anti-Stokes peaks, how the interferometer was calibrated at each temperature, and the AFM thickness uncertainty.

concerns.concern: The meaning of 'accumulated spectra' (acquisition time and number of scans) and how the error bars in Figs. 3b and 4b were obtained are unclear.
concerns.quote: Please clarify "accumulated spectra" (acquisition time and number of scans) and how error bars in Figs. 3b and 4b were obtained.

concerns.concern: The magnitude of the effect is quoted inconsistently as ~5.5% and ~6%.
concerns.quote: The magnitude is quoted as both "~5.5%" (Abstract, Fig. 4) and "~6%" (pp. 15, 17).

concerns.concern: The Fig. 3d caption omits the temperature, the magnetic state used and the q range.
concerns.quote: The Fig. 3d caption should state the temperature and magnetic state used, and the q range.

concerns.concern: The Methods give a Raman temperature range of 77–300 K, but Fig. 2 covers only 90–290 K.
concerns.quote: Methods quote a Raman temperature range of 77–300 K, while Fig. 2 covers 90–290 K.

concerns.concern: The axes of Fig. 2a are mislabelled.
concerns.quote: In Fig. 2a the axes are mislabelled: the x-axis should be Raman shift and the y-axis intensity.

concerns.concern: The text refers to 'red spheres' while the Fig. 3 caption says 'red circles'.
concerns.quote: The text refers to "red spheres" while the Fig. 3 caption says "red circles".

concerns.concern: There are typos and wrong terms or units: 'Temperaure', 'REFRENCES', 'electrodynamic' for 'elastodynamic', and 'ms⁻¹'.
concerns.quote: "linear electrodynamic equation" should be "elastodynamic"

concerns.concern: Ref. 19 has a garbled author list, and the spin-correlation notation on p. 16 is mis-typeset.
concerns.quote: Ref. 19 has a garbled author list. The notation ⟨S_i·S_j⟩ is mis-typeset on p. 16.
